function: p. 5-6: Over-the-air aggregation of federated model updates, using lattice-coded digital transmission and a two-layer multi-antenna server receiver that decodes an integer combination of quantized updates.
system: p. 3, 10: K=30 single-antenna devices, server with M=30 antennas, uplink multiple-access channel, no RIS; baseband model, no frequency band stated.
method: p. 4, 10: CNN classifier trained with federated learning (local SGD, FedAvg-style); aggregation by the proposed lattice-coded scheme with closed-form equalizer and convexified integer-coefficient selection.
data_channel: p. 10: Simulated Rayleigh fading, gain exp(5) with uniform phase, 20 realizations; MNIST and Fashion-MNIST for the learning task, same channel model for training and testing.
test_conditions: p. 10-11: One Rayleigh model for training and testing; figures sweep local iterations, antennas M, devices K, lattice scaling and code, with i.i.d. or non-i.i.d. data; test-set accuracy.
baselines: p. 11: Ideal UVeQFed [28] (orthogonal, error-free), OTA-CSIT [14] (power control with CSIT), BFEL [22] (blind over-the-air); all earlier published designs, no simple heuristic.
metrics: p. 10-11: Test accuracy versus global round (Figs. 5-11); analytical optimality gap (Theorem 3, p. 8); decoding and quantization MSE as design metrics (pp. 6-7).
complexity: none; p. 12 only says implementation and decoding complexity grows with lattice dimension, with no order, operation count or runtime.
openness: none; no code or data link in the paper; it uses public MNIST and Fashion-MNIST (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "channel gain with Rayleigh fading"; custom Rayleigh simulator with uniform phase, no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "Performance is gauged by the learning accuracy in relation to the test dataset"; every setting (K, M, tau, rho) uses the same channel model and no unseen condition is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "Among the evaluated benchmarks are ideal UVeQFed [28], OTA-CSIT [14], and BFEL [22] schemes"; test accuracy compared in Figs. 9-10. See notes.
q4_support: p. 12: "the complexity of implementation and decoding increases accordingly"; qualitative only, and p. 6 gives only the resource efficiency 1/K, a signaling cost.
q5_support: p. 10: "classifying images from two datasets of standard MNIST and Fashion-MNIST"; learning-task datasets only, the channel is simulated, and no code or data link appears.
notes: Include, area 7: the paper proposes over-the-air aggregation for federated learning with lattice codes over digital modulation (abstract p. 1; model and receiver pp. 5-6), so the learned element is the FL-trained CNN and the function is the aggregation. The server has M antennas (p. 3), so the single-antenna rule does not apply. Results are test-accuracy curves (pp. 10-11). q3 is borderline and judged met: all three baselines are FL schemes. OTA-CSIT [14] is the optimization-based power-control and device-selection design described on pp. 1-2 and BFEL [22] is an earlier published aggregation design, whereas ideal UVeQFed [28] is the orthogonal, classical transmission reference. The reviewer should confirm this reading of the non-learned comparator.
